title: Canonical support coefficient comparison at identity
statement: Let $s$ be any scheme, let $A,B$ be finite commutative rings, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be any ring map. For each identity compactification $d=(j,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], construct $\beta_{A,d}:F_{A,d}\simeq\operatorname{id}$ by the section-normalized clopen comparison of [lem-sp-clopen-section-component], its K-injective-preservation clause, the canonical derived comparison for an exact functor preserving K-injectives, and derived identity. Here $F_{A,d}$ is the actual ambient support candidate of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. Write $c_0=(\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id})$. For the actual derived coefficient extension $T_\varphi$ and published support coefficient map $\alpha_\varphi$ of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], every $K\in D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ satisfies $\alpha_{\varphi,K}\,;\,\beta_{B,c_0,T_\varphi K}=T_\varphi(\beta_{A,c_0,K})$. This is an equation of the specified canonical maps, including nonflat maps and zero coefficient rings.

proof.text: The open part of a compactification of id_s has clopen image because id_s is proper. Apply clopenSectionComponent to p,j and pj=id_s. Its section equation determines the underived isomorphism e:p_*j_! ≅ id; it also proves that j_! preserves K-injectives. Define beta by deriving e and inserting the exact-precomposition and derived-identity comparisons. This is the complete Lean construction pointIdentitySupportIso.

At c_0 the component restriction in e is the canonical identity restriction. The realization square for scalar restriction is identity on scalar-unit sections; the open restriction square is the unique adjunction-unit comparison; the proper restriction square is characterized on K-injective resolutions. Thus after the beta identifications the published support restriction comparison sends every section to itself. Check on a K-injective representative and a K-injective resolution of its scalar restriction; the comparison equations cancel their quasi-isomorphisms. Naturality and essential surjectivity extend the equality to every derived object.

Transpose this identity square through the actual derived tensor/restriction adjunctions used to define exceptionalFiniteSupportExtensionMap. The unit/counit triangle identities give alpha_phi,K followed by beta_B,TK equal to T(beta_A,K). Derive tensor on K-flat representatives, so no flatness of phi is needed. The same computation handles identity maps and zero rings.

theorem point_identity_support_normalization (s : Scheme.{u})
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory s A) :
    (exceptionalFiniteSupportExtensionMap φ (Compactification.ofIsProper (𝟙 s))).app K ≫
        (pointIdentitySupportIso s B (Compactification.ofIsProper (𝟙 s))).hom.app
          ((exceptionalCoefficientExtension φ s).obj K) =
      (exceptionalCoefficientExtension φ s).map
        ((pointIdentitySupportIso s A (Compactification.ofIsProper (𝟙 s))).hom.app K)
